title: Raynaud affineness for flat groups over a DVR
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G$ be an $S$-group scheme, meaning an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Suppose $G\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $G_K=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change] is affine, then $G$ is affine. Here an affine scheme means one isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme]. No smoothness, connectedness, excellence, henselianity, or perfectness of the residue field is assumed.

source.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.1, PDF p.5, statement and Raynaud proof; read online. This is the alternative affineness reference in Conrad Theorem 5.3.5, printed p.166. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-trait-group-finite-smooth-cover] to obtain a faithfully flat local DVR extension $R\to R'$ with algebraically closed residue field, and a finite surjective group homomorphism $q:N\to G_{R'}$, where $N$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $R'$. Write $L=\operatorname{Frac}R'$. The affine generic fibre $G_K$ remains affine over $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and $q_L$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]; hence $N_L$ is affine by part (b) of the latter. We will prove $N$ affine and then descend this conclusion.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, printed p.5, smooth reduction and affine-chart construction; online source, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Smoothness makes $N$ flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-trait-group-affinization] over $R'$: with $A=\Gamma(N,\mathcal O_N)$ and $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the canonical $u:N\to H$ is an $R'$-group homomorphism. The ring $A$ is not assumed finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], separatedness and finite type over the affine base imply that $N$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, printed p.5, smooth reduction and affine-chart construction; online source, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Take the finite global principal affine cover $N=\bigcup_jN_{f_j}$ from [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-principal-translate-cover]. For every $j$, [lem-a1-affine-principal-affinization-isomorphism] identifies $u^{-1}D(f_j)$ with $N_{f_j}$ and identifies its restriction with an isomorphism onto $D(f_j)\subset H$. These restrictions are restrictions of the same morphism $u$, so their inverse isomorphisms agree on overlaps; gluing them gives $N\simeq\bigcup_jD(f_j)$. Thus $u$ is an open immersion. It is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] applied to $N\to H\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$: $N\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is quasi-compact by finite type, and $H\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is affine, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Affine principal chart comparison, Tag 01P8; glue the inverses on their common restrictions. The existence of the cover follows the cited online Proposition 3.1.

proof.text: Let $\pi$ be a uniformizer of $R'$ and $k$ its residue field. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], base change of the open immersion $u$ to $k$ identifies $u_k:N_k\to H_k$ with an open immersion: it is the inclusion of the inverse image of the open subset $u(N)$ in $H_k$. The group homomorphism $u_k$ is a morphism of absolute groupoids over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, by taking both source and target maps to be the structure morphism. Apply [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-open-image-closed] to conclude that $u_k(N_k)$ is closed in $H_k$. Since $H_k=V(\pi\cdot1_A)$ is closed in $H$, the subset $u(N)\cap V(\pi\cdot1_A)=u_k(N_k)$ is closed in $H$. This uses no finite-type assertion for $H_k$.

source.place: Tag 04Q6, lemma-open-image-is-closed; open-immersion base change is Schemes Tag 01JY. A group scheme is an absolute groupoid over the point.

proof.text: For $j=u:N\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $f=\pi\cdot1_A$, we have a quasi-compact immersion by step 3. Its inverse image of $D(f)$ is $N_L$, because $D_R(\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a DVR, and $N_L$ is affine by step 1. Step 4 proves that $u(N)\cap V(f)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-immersion-principal-affineness], which proves that $N$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0ABH, lemma-get-affine; apply the quasi-compact immersion criterion with the uniformizer.

proof.text: Now [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-affine-target] applied to $q:N\to G_{R'}$ proves $G_{R'}$ affine. The base morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a singleton fpqc covering, as supplied by [lem-sfb-trait-group-finite-smooth-cover]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, then [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2), to obtain that $G$ is affine.

source.place: Descent of affine morphisms, Tag 02L5; finite-surjective descent of affine schemes is Tag 01ZT in limits.tex. This is the descent reduction in the first paragraph of the online Proposition 3.1.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of the smooth reduction and principal affine charts from Prasad–Yu Proposition 3.1 (online, local archive WANTED), followed by Stacks Tags 04Q6 and 0ABH instead of any forbidden source.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-0bbffe5a7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all three new nodes and every cited statement in full, and the review is in review.md. There is no local copy of Prasad–Yu, so I fetched qrg.pdf online. Its Prop. 3.1 (p.5) proof and the appendix's Cor. A.4 (p.29) and A.9/A.10 (pp.31–32) match the route: reduce by Cor. A.4 to a finite smooth normalization over a strictly henselian base, form Spec Γ(G) as a group, cover G by the BLR principal chart and its G(R)-translates, then descend by Chevalley and fpqc descent. The delivery drops the source's SGA3 VI_B 11.11 and Hopf-flatness ending. It proves N affine instead with Stacks 04Q6 (an open image of a morphism of groupoids over a field is closed) and 0ABH (lemma-get-affine), both read in more-groupoids.tex at lines 1459–1533 and 2769–2803. This replacement is correct, needs no finite type for H_k and no surjectivity of u, and cites no SGA. finite-smooth-cover: true by Cor. A.4 with its third bullet and the A.9 extension to an algebraically closed residue field. The normalization of G_red composed with G_red → G_{R′} is finite and surjective, and Cor. A.4 has no affineness or generic-smoothness hypothesis. flat-trait-group-affinization: I checked A⊗A ≅ Γ(G×G) myself, using a finite affine cover, flat base change and torsion-free hence flat A. principal-translate-cover: the BLR seed (u_f iso ⇔ G_f affine by 01P8) plus Hensel lifting at rational points gives the cover. The statement is true without connectedness, but I could not read BLR itself (WANTED). Steps 1–6 use their cited statements correctly: finite permanence (b) in the right direction, qcqs before 01P8, the Nagata quasi-compactness triangle with an affine H, the open-immersion base change, the three 0ABH hypotheses, and 01ZT, 02L5 and permanence (2). Small cases tested: the trivial group, μ_p in residue characteristic p, disconnected constant groups, a smooth group with disconnected special fibre, and an imperfect residue field. The candidates group-model-potential-smooth-normalization, raynaud-faltings-normalized-reduction, trf-reduced-fibre-modification and group-finite-translate-cover are not duplicates. This is a first split with no re-split note, there are no cycles, and the tool_uses are general scheme theory, accepted. Minor, no change: the new nodes' source.document points to a local PDF that does not exist yet (WANTED), and citations.json is mentioned in the report but not in the commit.
